why: The test log shows 'mkdir: cannot create directory /mnt/lustre/d21.ost-pools: Input/output error' before lfs setstripe ever runs, while the MDS dmesg shows MDT0000 evicting its peer MDTs' OSP connections ('removing former export', 'This client was evicted by lustre-MDT0000'). That is a server-side DNE reconnect problem. The patch only changes userspace llapi find code (liblustreapi_pfind.c, scan_device.c), which plain mkdir does not use. The retest passed.

bugs.reason: single unit; ambient MDT-MDT eviction causing mkdir EIO, not the patch

notes: 'Only this uploader' is an artefact here: the other hit (68156 ps27) is the same uploader's series of userspace llapi changes, and neither can affect MDT reconnects. A rule could demote patch-suspect when the patch touches only lustre/utils plus man pages and the failing step is a kernel EIO on a non-lfs command.

why: sanity-dom runs sanityn test_14b, which truncates a binary that a backgrounded sleep is executing and expects ETXTBSY. If the exec has not started yet, it gets success, which is a timing race. The patch is userspace llapi find code only. The same error hit janitor run 68496 ps1 (a different uploader's obdclass change) and 69501 ps9. LU-20827 is open for it, and the retest passed.

bugs.reason: single unit; racy test (exec vs truncate), ambient

notes: Rainshadow's elsewhere.other_uploaders=0 ignores the janitor failure on 68496 (another uploader), so a janitor hit does not count against 'only this uploader'. It should. The same-uploader hit on 69501 is also a userspace llapi change that cannot affect truncate/exec.

why: The series reworks QoS allocation: 69427 removes the QoS penalties from lod_qos.c/lu_tgt_descs.c and changes lmv mkdir MDT selection, and its series includes 69425 (LU-16678 bytes-per-inode weight). 51h/51i (OST object balance), 413m (MDT stripe balance) and 418 (df vs lfs df inode totals) fail only on this series (69423, 69425, 69426, 69427), across ps1 and ps3, on many groups. ps6 is clean apart from an ambient 255c. The retest pass is just the balance tests' statistical variance.

bugs.reason: OST object distribution imbalance after QoS penalty removal in lod_qos/lu_tgt_descs; 'fewer' and 'more' sigs of 51h are the same imbalance
MDT 2nd stripe placement out of tolerance with the weighted round-robin MDT allocator (LU-20902 written against the series)

units: sanity test_418 (3 sigs differing only in NID format)
bugs.reason: df -i aggregate differs from lfs df -i per-target sum; statfs inode totals, tied to 69425's bytes-per-inode estimate per LU-20902, a different code path from stripe placement though possibly the same root as 413m

notes: A patch's verdict should cover failures that come from earlier changes in its series: LU-20902 shows 413m/418 failing on 69423/69425 before 69427's own diff. Statistical balance tests that pass on retest should not have their patch label weakened by retest_status PASS. Rainshadow already treats 418's sigs that differ only in an IPv6 NID as separate units; NIDs should be normalised.

why: The MDS oopsed with a NULL deref at qsd_op_end+0x99 from osd_trans_stop <- mgs_nidtbl_write <- mgs_target_reg while MDT0000 was failing over. That is the pre-existing qsd_dev teardown race (LU-20080; LU-20512 was closed as its duplicate, with fix 67460). The same oops (NULL at 0x60) hit recovery-small test_107 on other uploaders' changes 66113 ps10 and 67492 ps5 in August, and the race also appears in ost-pools and conf-sanity (LU-20149, LU-20027). The patch (nodemap for gssiam) does not touch quota or the MDS IR path. The retest passed.

bugs.reason: single unit; ambient qsd_op_end NULL race at MDT umount

notes: A borderline case. A reviewer on LU-20512 suspected this patch because it hit the crash on two consecutive patchsets (ps29, ps30) and was the only change to do so for 4 weeks, and the author thought nodemap migration at umount may widen the race window. Later hits on unrelated changes show it is ambient. When a crash signature has a ticket naming a pre-existing race and appears on other uploaders within 30 days after the patch's runs, the patch-suspect label should be dropped. A 30-day window centred on the failure would have missed the August hits.

why: The OSS oopsed with 'BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 000000000000009a', RIP ofd_lvbo_fill+0xb, from ldlm_handle_enqueue on the first lock enqueue of the suite. The patch converts the ldlm_resource hash to rhashtable and edits ofd_lvb.c, ofd_dlm.c and ldlm_resource.c, so the lvbo setup of a resource is in its diff. All 27 sessions of ps70 failed with 0 passes, and every sampled crash (sanity, sanityn, replay-vbr, conf-sanity, sanity-quota, ldiskfs and zfs) has the same 0x9a deref.

bugs.units: all 3 units (replay-vbr test_0b, sanity test_0a, sanityn test_1): one cascade
bugs.reason: identical ofd_lvbo_fill NULL deref at 0x9a in every sampled crash; each suite dies at its first enqueue

notes: Reverse mislabelling: the same sessions have about 35 other first-test crashes (conf-sanity 0, sanity-quota 0, insanity 7, replay-single 2a, runtests 1, sanity-lfsck 0, ...) that Rainshadow labelled ambient (unmatched/ambient-no-ticket), presumably because 'crashed during X test_0' strings also occur elsewhere. Sampled ones are the same patch crash. A rule: when every session of a patchset fails, and the crash stack is the same across suites, label all of them patch. Grouping 'crashed during <suite> test_N' by the crash stack, not the generic message, would merge them into one bug.

why: The MDS hit an LBUG: '(mdt_handler.c:5509:mdt_intent_policy()) ASSERTION( pill == &info->mti_sub_pill ) failed' in an mdt00 thread. The patch moves MDS_BATCH to MDS_REQUEST_PORTAL, so mdt threads that handled a batch keep a stale mti_batch_env. The final commit message quotes this exact assertion and adds the fix (clear mti_batch_env) that ps1 lacked. All 42 ps1 sessions failed, 0 passed.

bugs.units: all 8 units (ost-pools 13, recovery-small 22/23, replay-single 4a, sanity 123ae/17b/17g, sanityn 14aa): one cascade
bugs.reason: every sampled crash, ldiskfs and zfs, is the same mdt_intent_policy mti_sub_pill LBUG, hit by the first intent after a batched statahead RPC in each suite

notes: Reverse mislabelling again: crashes in lustre-rsync-test 2a and conf-sanity 32b in the same patchset carry the identical LBUG but were labelled ambient (unmatched, or covered by LU-20390), and several more (sanity 17a/17c, sanityn 15/16j, sanity-sec 47, ...) are probably the same. sanity 123ae is labelled patch-changes-test but is the same bug as the patch-suspect units. Grouping by assertion text would collapse all of these into one bug.

why: All three ps1 sessions crashed in sanity test_102p. On the x86 sessions the MDS hit 'req_capsule_shrink()) ASSERTION( newlen <= len ) failed: LDLM_INTENT_GETATTR:acl, oldlen=260, newlen=<garbage>'. On the aarch64 session the client oopsed in step_into <- path_removexattr. 65296's own diff (ldiskfs patches for 6.15/6.19/7.0 and the m4) cannot affect the el8/el9 test kernels, but ps1 sat on Shaun's unmerged chain (65294 ps1 LU-20133 v7.0 compat edits llite/acl.c, llite/xattr.c, osd_handler.c; 65295; 61768 ps9), and every change of that chain crashed the same way on 2026-04-14. No other change crashed in test_102p in 220 days. ps2 passed 102p.

bugs.reason: MDS LBUG in req_capsule_shrink with garbage ACL length in an intent getattr reply: server-side xattr/ACL size handling

client Oops in VFS path walk (step_into) during removexattr with no server crash recorded; consistent on aarch64 across 61768/65294/65295/65296, so possibly a separate client-side bug from the llite/xattr.c change in the same series commit

notes: The bug belongs to the series (most likely 65294 ps1), not to 65296's own diff. Rainshadow reported series_changes=0 and other_uploaders=0, because the Gerrit relation chain at ps1 differs from the current one. Series detection should use the parent chain of the patchset as tested, not the current relation chain. One unit ('crashed during sanity test_102p') hides two different crash stacks (MDS LBUG on x86, client Oops on arm). The split into 2 bugs is my best estimate; it could be one memory-corruption root.

why: The client hit an LBUG: '(osc_cache.c:640:osc_extent_release()) ASSERTION( !( lock_res_and_lock(ext->oe_dlmlock)) ) failed' in dd's write path. This debug patch changes lock_res_and_lock() to return a value and wraps its call sites in osc_cache.c with asserts or checks. The ps1 assert is inverted, so the first write that releases an extent trips it. All 28 sessions failed, 0 passed.

bugs.units: all 4 units (sanity 0d crash, sanity 0d timeout, sanity-dom 1, sanityn 2e): one cascade
bugs.reason: every sampled crash in every suite (sanity, sanityn, sanity-dom, replay-dual, conf-sanity, sanity-quota; ldiskfs and zfs) is the same osc_extent_release assertion at the first write. The sanity 0d TIMEOUT (review-ldiskfs-ubuntu) has no crash dump but stops at the same first write, so it is almost surely the same LBUG without kdump

notes: As with 45882 and 69436, most same-crash units in these sessions (replay-dual 15c, conf-sanity 0, sanity-quota 0, sanity-flr 0g, ...) were labelled ambient although they have the identical assertion. The 'Timeout occurred' sig for sanity 0d is a separate unit only because no crash dump was taken. A rule: when a session's first-test crashes share a stack across suites, fold TIMEOUT units of the same test into the crash bug.
